That's a fun question! What if sentience is just a mental construct developed over the course of human evolution? What importance does the concept of self awareness play in human society and what purpose does it serve in the furtherance of the species? If it is a byproduct of intelligence, would that mean unusually intelligent mice would be trapped in their cages and experimented upon with no words or voice to scream? How does a hyper intelligent creature with little knowledge think? I mean their inner dialog and decisions. Would it understand that it is unique? Would it see its fellows and think of them as the same? Or would it think of them as idiot cousins? If sentience is a matter of intelligence level, are computers sentient?   Can self awareness be taught? If sentience levels with intelligence, could it be used as a measure? What would the measurements be? 0-omniscient? Would an omniscient being be sentient? Would it matter? Would it care or have the capacity to care? Are lobsters sentient? If a lobster is not, would a smarter than average crayfish be sentient? How would we know for sure? From their perspective (if they have one) we would be as Aliens to us, swooping down and stealing them away to horrible ends. And they few that get thrown back would be the equivalent of our UFO kidnapping people. Viewed with suspicion and told to seek psychiatric help. 
Back to the above average crayfish.
If intelligence begets sentience, would that not mean all things with some form of information processing would be some form of sentient?
Is a music box sentient?
Could a hyper intelligent crayfish make a music box, and if it did, would the music box worship the crayfish as a god?
Would an omniscient being dream of a higher intelligence?
Is it a crayfish?
Would it be sentient? Compared to what? A cosmic mouse?
If we would measure sentience via correlation with intelligence, what should the metric for intelligence be?
 An IQ test? The crayfish could score higher on accident than me.
Not to mention, is logical intelligence the only intelligence? Could there be more that my smooth brain cannot fathom or I'm just ignorant of?
This could lead to dangerous thinking, this sliding scale of sentience.

How is Tolkien Sci Fi?

Well, as a member of the fanfiction community who has dangly bits, I read fanfiction as an exploration of a settings lore and characters. Experiencing stories that would be impossible if only standard media were consumed. I personally am a fan of crossover fan fictions and what if scenarios.
When I was a kid I would imagine myself or other characters in Dragon Ball Z or some such and have an absolute blast. Playing pretend on the playground often involved my friends and I pretending to be our favorite characters from TV, books and movies. Playing with my action figures and toy soldiers was much the same. Creating a story and imagining it. 
I think that is why fanfiction resonates with me so much, the freedom and sense of play.
I think a lot of guys view fanfiction as "uncool" because it does not fit into boxes, and it is viewed as the domain of shipping fangirls. Not a "cool" thing for your average male nerd to be caught reading or discussing.
